expectation: Glucose will enter through the existing transporter, perhaps beginning its breakdown.

effect: Glucose enters through the carrier and is broken down in the cytosol, producing some ATP and pyruvate for mitochondria. The next goal is to remake ATP and pump ions.
reaction: The cytosolic ATP arrow usefully shows that ATP production isn't confined to mitochondria.
reason: Oxygen is the only offered combination and should help the mitochondria process the fuel toward the ATP goal.
expectation: Oxygen will support mitochondrial processing of the glucose-derived fuel, possibly setting up ATP production.

effect: Oxygen receives electrons at the end of the mitochondrial pathway and becomes part of water; fuel supplies the energy. The next step is to remake ATP.
reaction: The distinction between oxygen's role and fuel's role is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and directly addresses the ATP goal.
expectation: ADP and phosphate will combine to form ATP using energy from respiration, though the intermediate mechanism is not yet shown.

effect: The result shows how electron flow builds an H⁺ gradient that drives ATP production, linking respiration to the pump goal.
reaction: The two-panel depiction makes the intermediate mechanism clearer.
reason: The ion pump is the only offered combination and should put the remade ATP to work.
expectation: The pump will use ATP to move sodium and potassium across the membrane, likely against their concentration gradients.

effect: The completed pump links ATP use to maintaining sodium and potassium concentration differences, completing the chapter's goals.
reaction: The contrast between passive sodium flow and ATP-powered pumping is satisfying and clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Remaking ATP was most worthwhile: the planned two-panel illustration connects electron flow, the hydrogen-ion gradient and ATP production rather than leaving the mechanism as a slogan.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequence offered only one combination at each decision, so there was little opportunity for meaningful choice, even though the explanations were useful.

surprise.text: The first result highlighted ATP production in the cytosol as well as fuel delivery to mitochondria, clarifying that ATP production is not confined to mitochondria.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt purposeless; each followed the stated goal, although compatibility was supplied rather than discovered.

continue.text: I would continue to see how later constructions connect cell processes to larger structures, though I would hope for more meaningful choices.
